chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a mukatab (a slave who has contracted for manumission for a certain sum) who pays part of his manumission money, then dies, leaving a son by his concubine. He said: 'If it was stipulated that the son would remain enslaved, the son becomes enslaved along with his mother. And if it was not stipulated, the son becomes free, and he pays the remainder of the manumission money to the master, and the son inherits what remains.'

key_terms.اُشْتُرِطَ: It was stipulated (as a condition in the contract).
key_terms.جَارِيَتِهِ: His concubine (female slave with whom he has sexual relations).
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his freedom.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission contract or the agreed-upon sum for freedom.

ai.seo_question: What happens to the son of a mukatab if the father dies after paying part of the manumission fee?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance and manumission status of a mukatab’s son upon the father's death, a key issue in Shia jurisprudence regarding conditional manumission. It establishes that unless the master explicitly stipulated the son's continued enslavement, the son inherits freedom and the residual estate while assuming liability for the remaining debt, reflecting the principle of *asl al-bar'ah* (presumption of freedom) in the absence of specific conditions. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on protecting the offspring of enslaved persons from automatic servitude unless contractually bound.
